Let <MATH_0001> be a smooth morphism of algebraic spaces.
If <MATH_0002> is reduced, then <MATH_0003> is reduced. If <MATH_0004> is surjective
and <MATH_0005> is reduced, then <MATH_0006> is reduced.

Choose a commutative diagram
<MATH_0001>
where <MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003> are schemes, the vertical arrows are surjective and
<ACCENT_0001>tale, and <MATH_0004> is surjective <ACCENT_0002>tale. Observe that <MATH_0005> is
a reduced algebraic space if and only if <MATH_0006> is a reduced scheme
by our definition of reduced algebraic spaces in
Properties of Spaces, Section <REF_0001>.
Similarly for <MATH_0007> and <MATH_0008>. 
The morphism <MATH_0009> is a smooth morphism of schemes, see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Since being reduced is local for the smooth topology for
schemes (Descent, Lemma <REF_0003>)
we see that <MATH_0010> is reduced if <MATH_0011> is reduced.
On the other hand, if <MATH_0012> is surjective, then <MATH_0013> is
surjective and in this case if <MATH_0014> is reduced, then <MATH_0015> is reduced.
